name: Static Interference

phase_0.boundary_condition: The spatial volume of the interference field where phase coherence is maintained.

VINIT.justification: The origin of the electromagnetic field before spatial propagation begins.

TANCH.justification: The final boundary where the spatial distribution of energy is fixed and measured.

AFWD.justification: The forward movement of the wavefront through the medium toward the target.

AREV.justification: The relative delay or backward shift in phase relative to the reference wave.

CLINK.justification: The sequential accumulation of phase shifts along a specific trajectory.

IMSCRIB.justification: The self-consistent state of a wave cycle at a specific spatial coordinate.

FSPLIT.justification: The separation of a single coherent wavefront into two distinct spatial paths.

FFUSE.justification: The recombination of the two paths into a single resultant field amplitude.

EVALT.justification: The state where phase alignment results in maximum intensity.

EVALF.justification: The state where phase opposition results in minimum intensity.

ENGAGR.justification: The simultaneous presence of multiple spatial frequencies held in a single complex lattice.

IFIX.justification: The permanent fixation of the interference pattern into a physical medium.

phase_3.void_description: The dark state before the activation of the coherent source.
phase_3.true_description: Bright fringe representing maximum constructive reinforcement.
phase_3.false_description: Dark fringe representing total destructive cancellation.
phase_3.both_description: The complete interference pattern containing the full gradient of phase relationships.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the coherent light source at the origin.
Establish the fundamental frequency and phase identity of the source.
Propagate the wavefront toward the beam splitter.
Divide the wavefront into two distinct optical paths.
Calculate the optical path length for the primary arm.
Anchor the primary arm as the reference phase for constructive potential.
Introduce a phase shift in the secondary arm relative to the primary.
Anchor the secondary arm as the candidate for destructive potential.
Recombine the two paths at the observation point to allow superposition.
Hold the resulting interference state as a spatial distribution of intensities.
Record the static fringe pattern onto the photographic emulsion.
Terminate the system at the physical boundary of the detector.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The physical geometry of the optical bench and component alignment.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Electromagnetic field coupling and phase synchronization.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The spatial coordinates of the interference fringes within the volume.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The constant velocity of light determining the simultaneous arrival of wavefronts.
phase_5.alfs_store: The Huygens-Fresnel principle governing wave propagation and interference.

phase_6.cycle_cost: Photon absorption and thermal dissipation at the observation plane.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Spatially modulated energy distribution in a fixed lattice.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The process is a reversible spatial redistribution of energy density without loss of coherence until the final measurement.
